title: Eternal decree frees elect by giving converting grace in time—not by suspending the law
source_text: XII. Ab aeterno quidem decrevit Deus electos, a poena peccatis ipsorum debita, immunes praestare; verum, non infringendo legem, cujus vi damnationi aeternae subjiciuntur, qui in peccato manent, nec ei renunciant; aut illos ab ista lege excipiendo: sed in tempore iis impartiendo gratiam, per quam in Christum credant, & ad Deum vere convertantur. Qua demum accepta, non prius, desinunt esse irae & damnationi aeternae obnoxii, sicut erant quum peccato inserviebant. Idque virtute ordinationis illius Evangelicae, qua Deus statuit a poenis peccati liberare, & pro justis habere, omnes illos qui in Christum viva fide crederent, a peccato sese averterent, & studium novae vitae amplecterentur. Juxta illud Pauli ad Romanos, Si confessus fueris ore tuo Dominum Jesum, & credideris in corde tuo quod Deus eum suscitavit ex mortuis, salvus eris. Rom. 10. 9. Et ad custodem carceris Philippensis, Crede in Dominum Jesum Christum, & salvaberis. Act. 16. 31. Quo spectat etiam illud Solomonis, Qui abscondit scelera sua non prosperabitur; qui autem confessus fuerit, & reliquerit ea, misericordiam consequetur. Prov. 28. 13. Et quod dicit Deus apud Ezechielem, Si impius egerit poenitentiam ab omnibus peccatis suis quae operatus est, & custodierit omnia praecepta mea, & fecerit judicium & justitiam; omnium iniquitatum ejus, quae operatus est, non recordabor: in justitia sua, quam operatus est, vivet. Numquid voluntatis meae est mors impii, dicit Dominus Deus, & non ut convertatur a viis suis, & vivat? Ezech. 18. 21. Unde est quod Petrus ad Judaeos dicit, Resipiscite, & convertite vos, ut deleantur peccata vestra. Et ad Simonem Magum, Poenitentiam age ab hac nequitia tua, & roga Deum, si forte remittatur tibi haec cogitatio cordis tui.
pass_a_gloss: From eternity God indeed decreed to render the elect immune from the punishment due their sins; yet not by breaking the law by whose force those who remain in sin and do not renounce it are subjected to eternal damnation, nor by excepting them from that law: but by imparting to them in time the grace through which they believe in Christ and are truly converted to God. Only when that grace is received—not before—do they cease to be liable to wrath and eternal damnation as they were when they served sin. And that by virtue of that evangelical ordinance by which God determined to free from sin's penalties and hold as just all who would believe in Christ with living faith, turn from sin, and embrace the pursuit of a new life. According to Paul's word to the Romans: If you confess with your mouth the Lord Jesus and believe in your heart that God raised him from the dead, you will be saved (Rom 10:9). And to the Philippian jailer: Believe in the Lord Jesus Christ, and you will be saved (Acts 16:31). To this also looks Solomon's word: Whoever conceals his crimes will not prosper; but whoever confesses and forsakes them will obtain mercy (Prov 28:13). And what God says in Ezekiel: If the wicked turns from all his sins which he has done, and keeps all my commandments, and does judgment and righteousness, I will not remember any of his iniquities which he has done; in his righteousness which he has done he shall live. Have I any pleasure in the death of the wicked, says the Lord God, and not rather that he turn from his ways and live? (Ezek 18:21). Hence Peter says to the Jews: Repent and turn, that your sins may be blotted out. And to Simon Magus: Repent of this wickedness of yours, and ask God if perhaps this thought of your heart may be forgiven you.
pass_b_english: The eternal decree frees the elect by giving converting grace in time—not by voiding the law.
Scripture ties remission to living faith, repentance, and turning (Rom 10; Acts; Prov; Ezek).

choices.why: Decree works through converting grace, not law-suspension.
